# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Online: my.cigna.com | Phone: 1-800-244-6224

**From:**
Sawyer Alvarez
[My street address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-11**
- **Member name:** Sawyer Alvarez
- **Member ID:** W635441117
- **Reference number:** POC-A1F3D3C000-86797
- **Denied service:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
- **Requesting surgeon:** Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), State of Ohio
- **Governing policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty, effective 3/15/2026 — https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_0285_coveragepositioncriteria_total_ankle_arthroplasty.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) that my surgeon, Duval, MD, requested on my behalf. The notice dated 2026-08-11 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision, because the criteria published in the plan's own coverage policy are the criteria my medical records already meet.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe the notice gives me. The notice states my appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, and I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter (and/or submitting it through my.cigna.com, per the plan's instructions).

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty states:

> "Total Ankle Arthroplasty/Replacement/Revision Considered Medically Necessary when criteria in the applicable policy statements listed above are met:"

and it sets out the pathway that applies to me:

> "Food and Drug Administration (FDA)- approved/cleared device* is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy then lists those criteria, including:

> " is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration  interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy) • individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:"

Here is how each part of that language lines up with the records already in my file:

**Function-limiting at short distances, for at least three months.** The policy gives "limiting activity to two city blocks" as its own example. My records state that I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks. My symptoms are documented as 12 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest — four times the three-month minimum the policy sets.

**Failure of at least six months of conservative therapy.** The policy names "anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy." My records document NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance for 10 weeks, from 2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27, with 18 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. I also had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that gave only about two weeks of partial relief. The policy itself describes this kind of care when it states:

> "Conservative management typically consists of medications for pain control, limiting activity, the use of ankle braces to stabilize the joint, shoe modifications, heat, and physical therapy to control the pain associated with ankle arthrosis."

I did that care, over more than six months, and it did not work.

**No contraindications.** My records state that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

**Objective findings.** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken 2026-06-02 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. My examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

The policy states:

> "Where coverage for care or services does not depend on specific circumstances, reimbursement will only be provided if a requested service(s) is submitted in accordance with the relevant criteria outlined in the applicable Coverage Policy, including covered diagnosis and/or procedure code(s)."

I believe my request was submitted in accordance with those criteria. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the documentation in my file addresses each element the policy lists — the distance limitation and its duration, the six months of failed conservative therapy, the absence of contraindications, and the imaging and exam findings. The denial notice does not identify which of these criteria the records were found not to meet.

I would also note, for accuracy, that my request is for a total ankle replacement and not a revision procedure, so the policy's revision-arthroplasty statements are not the ones that govern my case.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Cigna to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-11 (reference POC-A1F3D3C000-86797) and authorize CPT 27702;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic surgery expertise;
3. If the denial is upheld, send me a written explanation identifying the specific criterion in Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty that my records were found not to meet, along with a copy of the criteria used and information about my further appeal rights, including external review.

I am attaching the supporting records referenced above: [list of records being enclosed — e.g., physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, 2026-06-02 radiology report, office notes from Duval, MD].

Thank you for taking a second look at this. Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address] if anything further would help your review.

Sincerely,

_________________________
Sawyer Alvarez
Member ID: W635441117
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
[My address]
[My phone number]

**Enclosures:** [List of enclosed records]
**cc:** Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

0285 Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for moderate to severe ankle pain secondary to failure of an implanted device (e.g., implant loosening, malpositioning, periprosthetic infection, periprosthetic fracture).
Revision Surgery Revision surgery may be necessary in the presence of failed arthroplasty.
Failed arthroplasty is typically suspected when pain occurs progressively over time and is persistent, indicating implant loosening and collapse.
Surgical management of failed TAR may include ankle arthrodesi s, revision arthroplasty, or amputation.
Revision total ankle arthroplasty for any other indication is considered not medically necessary.

Conservative management typically consists of medications for pain control, limiting activity, the use of ankle braces to stabilize the joint, shoe modifications, heat, and physical therapy to control the pain associated with ankle arthrosis.
When conservative management fails, ankle arthrodesis (AA) (fusion) has been the standard surgical treatment of choice to control the pain of severe ankle arthritis.
